scanner_finding.title: tomcat: Potential RCE and/or information disclosure and/or information corruption with partial PUT
scanner_finding.description:
Path Equivalence: 'file.Name' (Internal Dot) leading to Remote Code Execution and/or Information disclosure and/or malicious content added to uploaded files via write enabled Default Servlet in Apache Tomcat.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.2, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.34, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.98.
The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are 
known to be affected: 8.5.0 though 8.5.100. Other, older, EOL versions 
may also be affected.


If all of the following were true, a malicious user was able to view       security sensitive files and/or inject content into those files:
- writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default)
- support for partial PUT (enabled by default)
- a target URL for security sensitive uploads that was a sub-directory of a target URL for public uploads
- attacker knowledge of the names of security sensitive files being uploaded
- the security sensitive files also being uploaded via partial PUT

If all of the following were true, a malicious user was able to       perform remote code execution:
- writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default)
- support for partial PUT (enabled by default)
- application was using Tomcat's file based session persistence with the default storage location
- application included a library that may be leveraged in a deserialization attack

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.3, 10.1.35 or 9.0.99, which fixes the issue.

remediation.primary: Upgrade Apache Tomcat to a fixed version.

validation.version_check: Verify the running Tomcat version is fixed.
validation.behavioral_check: Verify that the vulnerable configuration or behavior is no longer present.

applicability.reason: The installed version of org.apache.tomcat:tomcat-catalina is 9.0.98, which falls within the affected range of 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.98 for CVE-2025-24813.

conditions.evidence: The environment configuration shows 'default_servlet.writes_enabled' is set to true and 'default_servlet.readonly' is set to false.
conditions.reason: The Default Servlet is explicitly configured to allow writes.

conditions.evidence: The environment configuration shows 'default_servlet.allowPartialPut' is set to true.
conditions.reason: Support for partial PUT is enabled by default in the configuration.

conditions.evidence: No evidence is provided regarding application routes or upload paths.
conditions.reason: The relationship between security-sensitive and public upload directories cannot be determined from the provided evidence.

conditions.evidence: No evidence is provided regarding application behavior or routes.
conditions.reason: It is unknown if an attacker can identify the names of sensitive files being uploaded.

conditions.evidence: No evidence is provided regarding application behavior or upload configuration.
conditions.reason: It is unknown if sensitive files are uploaded using the partial PUT method.

conditions.evidence: The environment configuration shows 'session_persistence.file_based_persistence' is true.
conditions.reason: The application is using Tomcat's file-based session persistence.
No libraries that could be leveraged in a deserialization attack were identified in the provided evidence.

rce_assessment.reason: While several prerequisites for RCE are met (writes enabled, partial PUT enabled, and file-based session persistence enabled), the required presence of a library for deserialization attacks was not found in the provided evidence.

information_disclosure_assessment.reason: The conditions for information disclosure or content injection cannot be fully evaluated because the upload path relationships and file upload behaviors are unknown.

remediation_analysis.root_cause: Path equivalence issues in the Default Servlet allow for potential unauthorized file manipulation when writes are enabled and partial PUT is supported.

remediation.reason: These versions contain the official vendor fix for CVE-2025-24813.
Disabling write capabilities for the Default Servlet mitigates the primary attack vector for both RCE and information disclosure.

validation: Verify the installed version of tomcat-catalina is 9.0.99 or higher (for the 9.x branch).
Re-run the Trivy scanner to ensure the vulnerability is no longer detected.
Confirm that 'default_servlet.readonly' is set to true in the production configuration.
unknowns: The specific application upload paths and their relationship to public directories.
Whether the application uses partial PUT for sensitive file uploads.
The presence of any libraries that might enable deserialization attacks if the library list is incomplete.
